source: User explicit review and request to record lessons
layout: clear focal subject, silhouette and material hierarchy
readable text and exact claims at delivery size
motion: action or state changes serve the argument
natural phrasing and clear reading holds
meaningful changes of shot scale, density or medium
picture and sound share important event times
reject: accidental blank frames or missing assets
repeated demo staging presented as a new treatment without a content reason
technical checks presented as aesthetic or listening approval
qa: representative real style frames before full production
key poses and actions over time
actual export with captions and mix
another subject and composition for new reusable techniques
skill_status: Bundled source baseline; runtime dependencies installed externally on use
voice_identity: Mature middle-aged mainland Chinese man, low, slightly gravelly, magnetic; stage-actor presence with natural non-broadcast delivery
performance_rule: Identity remains fixed; emotion, emphasis, pacing and phrasing are redesigned for genre, content and narrative beat every episode
pause_rule: Distinguish event closure from new reflective narration; preserve linked ideas; never add one fixed pause everywhere
component_reuse: Reuse techniques and suitable complete layouts; project-owned drawing and renderers may establish a new visual language.
component_necessity: For each instance, state what understanding would be lost if it were removed; omit redundant labels and avoid premature payoff information.
footage_uniqueness: One original moving shot per film. Include main frame, inset cards and blurred backgrounds. Renaming, cropping, retiming or using disjoint portions of the same shot does not count as new footage. Static identity portraits may repeat; distinct shots from the same film may be used.
caption_rule: Chinese subtitles use one line; English may use up to two. Split long speech into separate phrase-timed cues without shrinking or truncating.
